newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate edges higher to 7.00/30 pct.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate edges higher to 7.00/30 pct.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate edged up to 7.00/30 percent from against 6.50 percent, dealers said.
"We did 7.00/30 today, slightly higher," said a money market dealer.
The rate traded between 6.50 to 7.80 percent, which dealers said was a narrow band after the recent volatility and wild swings of interest rates.
Dealers said interbank rates had fallen near "normal" levels after being spiked some weeks ago following volatility caused by a run on the Thai baht which spilled over onto the ringgit.
Overall liquidity continued to improve, which dealers said was mainly from offshore money making a slow comeback this week.
Earlier, the active one-month rate was trade at 7.50 percent, down from 8.0 on Wednesday.
The one-, two- and three-week money were at 7.40/50 percent from 7.50/80 previously.
Three-month money was at 7.50/60 percent from 7.50/8.0.
The market continued its vigil on the release of Malaysia's first quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data and April money supply numbers, which could give clues to interest rate direction.
Bank Negara was expected to release the GDP data on Friday and money supply next week.
Economists expect the GDP growth to be around 8.0-8.2 percent, against 8.3 in the first quarter of 1996.
